title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cameron, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cameron, WV | Marshall County
metaDescription: Cameron, WV sits in Marshall County, one of the top Marcellus producers in the US. We buy mineral rights and royalty interests here, title-checked first.
heroLead: Cameron sits south of Moundsville in Marshall County, in the thick of some of the densest horizontal drilling anywhere in the Marcellus play.
intro: Marshall County's well count and pooled-unit density mean Cameron-area mineral tracts are more likely than most in the state to already be inside an active, multi-well unit. That changes the value equation, but it also means the paperwork behind any given interest is more likely to have gone through several rounds of pooling orders and amendments over the years.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Cameron directly, and we check the actual unit order and well count for your tract before naming a figure, because a unit with three producing wells doesn't value the same as one with a single legacy well.

sections.heading: Dense pooling changes the picture
paragraphs: Operators in Marshall County have pulled acreage from multiple original farm tracts into single large units, which means your decimal interest in a Cameron-area unit may be a small share of a large, multi-well pool rather than a large share of a single well. We calculate value from the actual unit order, not a rough county average.

sections.heading: Older farm tracts, newer pooling orders
paragraphs: Cameron's surrounding farmland was owned by families for generations before horizontal drilling arrived, and those original tracts have since been folded into modern spacing units. Tracing your interest from the current pooling order back to the original farm deed is part of confirming what you actually own.

sections.heading: Reading the royalty statement
paragraphs: If you're already receiving payments on a Cameron-area interest, the statement itself, decimal interest, unit name, deduction line items, tells us how the well is actually performing. We review that history before making an offer rather than relying on a general estimate.

faqs.question: How many wells are typically in a Cameron-area unit?
faqs.answer: It varies by unit, but Marshall County has some of the densest multi-well pads in the play. We check your specific unit order to confirm well count.

faqs.question: My royalty checks have gotten smaller over time. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, production naturally declines over a well's life. We factor current decline behavior into our evaluation rather than assuming payments stay flat.

faqs.question: Can you value my interest without me finding the paperwork myself?
faqs.answer: In most cases yes. We can locate the recorded unit order and lease history for your tract directly through the Marshall County Clerk's office.
